clue.text: Arrive bearing container of wine and join in

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the word for arrive holds the wine container within it

parts.note: to arrive is to come
a bin is a rack or store for wine bottles

explanation.surface: Someone turns up carrying a crate of wine and joins the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' looks like a direction or carrying a load; here it means holding, so the wine store goes inside. 'and' and the closing 'in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To combine things is to unite or merge them, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Areas for playing trendy pursuit with passion

parts.note: courts are areas for games like tennis
hip means trendy, fashionable

explanation.surface: Fashionable sports venues are pursued with enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Courtship is wooing, the ardent pursuit of a romantic partner.

clue.text: Young lady one takes on expedition

parts.note: miss is a young unmarried woman
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A young woman signs up for a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A mission is a journey with a purpose, such as a military or diplomatic expedition.

clue.text: At home in dry surroundings nomad is self-centred

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: in surroundings means the word for dry wraps round the word for nomad
in surroundings means the word for dry wraps round the word for nomad

parts.note: TT means teetotal, so dry
a rover is a wanderer or nomad

explanation.surface: A wanderer settled in an alcohol-free home becomes absorbed in himself.
explanation.definitionFit: An introvert is inward-looking, focused on their own thoughts.

clue.text: It was used to swear in odd parts of England

indicators.note: odd parts means the first, third, fifth and seventh letters are taken

explanation.surface: An oath once common in some quaint corners of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Egad is an archaic mild oath, a softened form of 'oh God'.

clue.text: Not far from Oxford place? Lack maturity needed

parts.note: to lack something is to want it
age is maturity, the state of being grown up

explanation.surface: An Oxfordshire town is described as lacking the maturity it needs.
explanation.walkthrough: WANTAGE is a market town in Oxfordshire, some miles south-west of Oxford; the question mark admits the definition is vague.
explanation.definitionFit: The town lies in Oxfordshire within easy reach of Oxford, so it is a place near that city.

clue.text: Arrival times for woeful children

parts.note: the nursery rhyme says the child born on one weekday is full of woe, so arrival means birth

explanation.surface: Timetable entries for unhappy youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'Monday's child' runs 'Wednesday's child is full of woe'; arrival is birth.
explanation.definitionFit: In the rhyme, babies born on that day of the week are destined for sorrow.

clue.text: You are reported missing from wild part of Africa

indicators.note: missing from means the sounds are removed from the word for wild

parts.note: natural means wild, uncultivated

indicators.note: reported means the phrase is heard as letters spoken

parts.note: you are, spoken quickly, sounds like the two letters U and R

explanation.surface: Someone is said to have vanished in the African wilds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You are' sounds like U R, removed from NATURAL. Natal was a South African province, now KwaZulu-Natal.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal is a region on South Africa's east coast.

clue.text: Notice lines going in the opposite direction

parts.note: an ad is a notice
verse is lines of poetry

explanation.surface: Someone spots road markings running the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse means contrary or opposing, as in adverse winds.

clue.text: Follow directions, girl!

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north
Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is told to obey instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come after, to follow as a result.

clue.text: Mounted group producing disturbance

parts.note: mounted means up, as on horseback
a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: A party on horseback causes a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: An upset is a disruption or disturbance, as in a stomach upset or a political shock.

clue.text: In confusion, didn't I save nameless extras?

indicators.note: confusion signals the letters of the words that follow are muddled into a new order
nameless tells us to drop the letter standing for name, N, from those words

explanation.surface: A flustered person asks whether they forgot to keep some unnamed bonus items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' removes N (name) from DIDNTISAVE, leaving DIDTISAVE, which 'In confusion' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Additives are substances added to food and the like, things extra to the basic ingredients.

clue.text: He will clothe part of coat with gold

parts.note: a tail is the rear flap of a tailcoat
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A coat's fabric is trimmed with gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor makes clothes for people, so he is the one who will dress them.

clue.text: Be my guest and experience informality

explanation.surface: A host urges a visitor to relax and enjoy a casual atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second half as FEEL (experience) plus FREE (unconstrained), a light cryptic reading beside the polite invitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are invitations to act without restraint: one is a polite permission, the other a description of relaxing unconstrained.

clue.text: Concentrated after van becomes hard to control

indicators.note: after places the word for concentrated behind the word for van

parts.note: the van is the vanguard, the front or head
strong means concentrated, as of a drink

explanation.surface: A delivery van driver finds the strong mix makes it hard to steer.
explanation.definitionFit: Headstrong means wilful and obstinate, difficult to manage.

clue.text: Take female to church for this reason

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone is told to escort a woman to church for some purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Hence is a formal word meaning therefore, as a consequence.

clue.text: Was someone willing to provide this sort of mortgage?

definitions.text: Was someone willing to provide this sort of mortgage?

parts.words: Was someone willing to provide this sort of mortgage?
parts.note: willing is read as making a will, so the clue asks what a bequest provides, and also names a type of home loan backed by an insurance policy

explanation.surface: A home buyer asks whether a lender was prepared to offer a particular kind of loan.
explanation.walkthrough: An endowment mortgage was a common British home loan repaid from a maturing insurance policy; 'willing' here means leaving a legacy.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift left by will is a bequest, and the same word names a mortgage repaid by an investment policy.

clue.text: Whatever the result, refuse to be drawn?

explanation.surface: Someone declines to commit, whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: refusing a draw leaves only those two outcomes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means regardless of outcome, and a player refusing to draw must end victorious or beaten.

clue.text: Man and woman joined in religious belief

parts.note: Theo is a man's name
Sophy is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A couple unite in a shared faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Theosophy is a mystical religious philosophy seeking knowledge of the divine.

clue.text: In cutting way, did something rude? Lady takes no notice

parts.note: pointing at people is thought rude, so the gesture is something rude done

indicators.note: takes no means the word for notice is removed from the word lady

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper

explanation.surface: A woman ignores someone who has made a rude gesture at her.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing AD from LADY leaves LY.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark made pointedly is sharp and barbed, aimed to wound like a cutting comment.

clue.text: Meanwhile one enters during school time

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'

indicators.note: enters means the numeral for one goes into the word for school time

parts.note: a term is a period of the school year
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone arrives in the middle of the school term.
explanation.definitionFit: In the interim means in the meantime, the period between events.

clue.text: Ideal environment in which artist's work is situated

definitions.text: in which artist's work is situated

explanation.surface: A gallery visitor admires the perfect alcove for a sculptor's piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is both an ecological or personal setting that suits perfectly and a wall recess where a statue stands.

clue.text: Church covers poor boy suffering from cold

indicators.note: covers places the church abbreviation on top in this down answer

parts.note: ill means poor, as in poor health
Ed is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A church provides blankets for a shivering lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilled means made very cold.

clue.text: Takes back what is written about pamphlets

parts.note: re means about or concerning
tracts are short pamphlets, often religious or political

explanation.surface: Someone withdraws a written comment on some leaflets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what is written' only links: RE and TRACTS read as a heading on writing about pamphlets.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract is to withdraw a statement, to take it back.

clue.text: Join together what's split? Exactly!

parts.note: rive is an old word meaning split or tear apart
to a T means exactly

explanation.surface: An exasperated speaker confirms that a broken thing must be mended.
explanation.definitionFit: To rivet pieces is to fasten them with metal pins.

clue.text: Former politician enters excellent defence plea

indicators.note: enters means the politician goes into the word for excellent

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI
Lib is a member of the old Liberal party

explanation.surface: An ex-politician makes a superb case in court.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is written as AI. The British Liberal Party merged into the Liberal Democrats in 1988, hence 'former'.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of having been elsewhere, a defence against a charge.

clue.text: Militant groups putting sign outside motorway

indicators.note: outside means the zodiac word goes round the letter for motorway

parts.note: Aries is a sign of the zodiac
M stands for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Activists put a placard beside a highway.
explanation.definitionFit: Armies are organised bodies of fighters, so they are groups ready for battle.

clue.text: Before noon, morning's first two rounds

parts.note: AM means ante meridiem, before noon

indicators.note: first two means only the opening pair of letters of the word is used

explanation.surface: Before midday, the early shots of the day are fired.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammo is short for ammunition, rounds being cartridges.

clue.text: Like some spineless creatures, mostly vile people with convictions

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word for vile people is dropped

parts.note: vermin is a word for despicable people
form is slang for a criminal record of convictions

explanation.surface: Most cowardly folk turn out to be lowlifes with criminal records.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue dropped 'vile'. VERMIN loses its last letter for 'mostly'; FORM is British slang for a criminal record.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermiform means worm-shaped, and worms are invertebrates, creatures with no backbone.

clue.text: Part of ship men dock

parts.note: OR is other ranks, the ordinary soldiers or men
to dock is to cut off, to lop

explanation.surface: Sailors moor at a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' suggests a harbour but means cut.
explanation.definitionFit: The orlop is the lowest deck of a sailing ship.

clue.text: Casual work can be attractive but not the second time

indicators.note: not the second tells us to remove the second occurrence of the letter for time

parts.note: tempting means attractive, alluring

explanation.surface: Freelance jobs can be appealing, though not when tried twice.
explanation.walkthrough: TEMPTING has two Ts; the second goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Temping is working as a temporary employee, short-term casual employment.

clue.text: Old meet outside terminus for public occasion

indicators.note: outside means the word for meet surrounds the word for terminus

parts.note: to meet a bill is to pay it
a terminus is an end

explanation.surface: Old friends gather beyond a railway terminus for a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meet' looks like a gathering of people, but it means settle, as in meeting a bill; 'outside' wraps it round the terminus word, and 'for' links.
explanation.definitionFit: An open day is when an institution admits the public to look round.
